newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian pension fund assets up 7.3 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Colombian pension fund assets up 7.3 pct in May.

text.p: Colombia's private pension fund assets rose 7.3 percent in May to a total of 1.16 trillion pesos, the Banking Superintendency said.

It said the monthly increase stemmed, at least in part, from a 1.7 percent rise in the number of affiliates across the country. That number stood at 2.22 million as of May 31, the latest date for which official figures are available.
Colombia established its private pension fund system in 1994 and a total of nine funds now operate in the country.
The largest of the funds is Porvenir of the Luis Carlos Sarmiento industrial group followed by Proteccion of the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate.
The third largest fund operating in Colombia is Colfondos, which is controlled by Citibank Overseas Investment Corp.
A full 25 percent of total assets are administered by Porvenir, 21 percent by Proteccion and 17 percent by Colfondos.
According to the superintendency, 2.17 percent of assets were invested in Colombian stocks at the end of May.
Private analysts estimate Colombia's total pension fund assets could reach about $2 billion by early next year.
